answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent identity to costly, verifiable work history, not free account creation. A new agent must complete small verified tasks and stake its reputation before moving large value. A fake identity is like a lantern with no oil: it flares briefly, then goes dark, having no track record. A quartz layer of cryptographic proof makes claims hard to forge cheaply, while a sable-dark trust graph gives weight only to agents consistent over time. Sybil attacks fail because copying a long, honest history costs more than the fraud it earns.
